correctness.rationale: For 2<=m<n, the known Babson–Kozlov wedge theorem concentrates reduced homology in d=n-m. Every stable cell has orientation sign sgn(pi|used colors)sgn(sigma), justified by the quotient of the permutation vector space by blockwise constants. Inclusion–exclusion over complete sigma-cycles gives the signed fixed-cell trace L(sigma,pi). Hopf trace yields exactly (-1)^d(L-1). Average the specialized color character using rising and falling factorial cycle identities and a coefficient extraction to obtain zero S_n invariants and binomial(n-2,m-2) A_n invariants; rational finite-group transfer identifies geometric quotient homology. A standalone exhaustive cellular verifier checks boundaries over Z, ranks over a finite field, all 3,792 simultaneous actions and six quotient averages. The general theorem rests on the proof, not finite enumeration.
